title: 塩の道を歩いた人 ― ガンジーと非暴力
style: 画風01・光彩のある劇場アニメ背景を基調にした歴史ドキュメンタリー
research_basis: Gandhi Heritage Portal: Dandi March chronology and original marchers
Government of India Dandi Path Heritage Management: March 12-April 6, 1930 route and Salt Law defiance
Press Information Bureau, Government of India: British salt monopoly, civil disobedience and later arrests
Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute at Stanford: Gandhi's direct influence on King's nonviolent method
timeline: March 12, 1930: Gandhi and seventy-eight original satyagrahis leave Sabarmati Ashram
March-April 1930: the group walks roughly 385 kilometers toward Dandi while crowds grow along the route
April 6, 1930: Gandhi breaks the Salt Law at Dandi by taking natural salt from the shore
May 1930 and later campaigns: Gandhi is arrested; arrest scenes must be separate from the Dandi shore
1947: India gains independence; the Salt March is one important contribution, not the sole cause
1950s-1960s: Martin Luther King Jr. studies and applies Gandhian nonviolent resistance in a distinct U.S. context
later decades: movements in many countries adapt nonviolent action to their own struggles

visual_anchors.gandhi: Mohandas Gandhi at age sixty in 1930: very slim Indian man, bald head with narrow gray fringe, small gray mustache, round wire spectacles, plain white hand-spun khadi dhoti and shawl, bamboo walking staff, composed but determined expression
visual_anchors.original_marchers: seventy-eight disciplined male satyagrahis of varied Indian regions and ages, simple white khadi clothing, walking in an orderly group rather than a military formation
visual_anchors.student: the same modern 17-year-old Japanese male student used in H040-H043, short black hair, navy school coat, gray scarf and black backpack
visual_anchors.salt_action: Gandhi stoops at the wet Dandi shore and lifts a small irregular lump or crust of natural salt-bearing mud; never a modern bag of table salt

history_accuracy: show the initial seventy-eight companions at Sabarmati before later roadside crowds join
do not place a giant crowd at the exact departure gate or imply that all later participants completed the whole route
show British salt control through period warehouses, officials, scales and guarded salt pans, without readable invented notices
show the salt tax burden through ordinary families purchasing a basic necessity, not through famine spectacle
the Dandi act is disciplined civil disobedience without weapons; police response may be tense but must not become an action battle
separate the April 6 salt-law breach from Gandhi's later arrest
do not depict the Salt March as single-handedly or immediately winning independence
King studies Gandhi's writings and method years later; Gandhi and King must not meet in the same room

composition.subtitle_safe_area: keep faces, hands, walking feet, salt, staff, documents and symbolic action above the lower 45 percent
composition.camera: one stable push, pull or hold per shot
composition.text: no readable generated signs, newspapers, maps, placards, dates, flags with lettering or quotations

avoid: photorealism, oil-paint texture, caricature, devotional halo or saint iconography
modern Indian clothing or infrastructure in 1930 scenes
military victory imagery, raised weapons or triumphant nationalist spectacle
Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr. physically meeting
clean commercial table salt in Gandhi's hand
a literal instant collapse of British rule at the beach
readable generated text, logos, watermarks or fake quotations
